### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **41** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c0cf65f79a7db985edc349d3615d3bb52d6362e`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 58 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c0cf65f79a7db985edc349d3615d3bb52d6362e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8b09292f6340d8ba3af48d6a2800c56a8c2b8d7e` — the merge of head `c3019504e02664d6e96c940a28dfdaebb28d0198` into base `4c0cf65f79a7db985edc349d3615d3bb52d6362e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8b09292f6340d8ba3af48d6a2800c56a8c2b8d7e && git checkout 8b09292f6340d8ba3af48d6a2800c56a8c2b8d7e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4c0cf65f79a7db985edc349d3615d3bb52d6362e c3019504e02664d6e96c940a28dfdaebb28d0198 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4c0cf65f79a7db985edc349d3615d3bb52d6362e && git merge --no-ff c3019504e02664d6e96c940a28dfdaebb28d0198

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c0cf65f79a7db985edc349d3615d3bb52d6362e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4c0cf65f79a7db985edc349d3615d3bb52d6362e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3557594b65debd8755e4e2c90385d781706f5540`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/mcp/src/action-confirmation-elicitation.ts, packages/mcp/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-action-confirmation-handoff-33690.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-confirmation-handoff-33690.test.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/objectql/src/record-title.ts, docs/adr/0011-actions-as-ai-tools.md (read in the cited code, not reviewed)

The face is semantic, not a narrowing (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic`); the four sections are judged as the brief sets them. Inputs: card #33712 with all five comments, the PR body and file list, the net diff against merge base `4bd3f240`, and the check-runs on the head (every run `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending). The SDK source is not in this checkout, so SDK behaviour is taken from the PR's pins that CI ran green on this head, not from a read of the SDK.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of a declared-gated `run_action` / `resume_run` call, stdio door, client advertised form-mode `elicitation`: right.** It moves from the hand-off (`pending_confirmation`) to one in-client question. `accept` falls through to the ordinary dispatch once; `decline`, `cancel`, `timed_out` are refused `428 ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` with `declined` / `cancelled` / `timed_out`, through the existing `confirmationRefusalOf`. These reasons are already members of the closed tuple on `main`; nothing is added to the spec.
- **Order (contract rule 2): right.** `admitResolvedAction` runs every gate, then the subject load; `confirmAdmittedAction` asks the caller-scope verdict (`refuseDeniedSubjectBeforeHandOff`) and only then the elicitor. On `resume_run` the elicit branch sits after steps 1 to 3 and after `refuseUnresumableAdmittedRun` (steps 4 and 5). One call site per door, so the person is asked at most once per call.
- **The caller's `confirm` (rule 5): right.** The elicit branch is reached only through `aiDoorConfirmation`, which does not take the request; `elicitActionConfirmation` takes the elicitor and the subject and nothing else. No path reads the member.
- **AI service account (rule 6): right.** Refused in `admitResolvedAction` before the subject load, and in `resumeAdmissionRefusal` before the elicit branch. Pinned on both tools.
- **Non-capable client and the Streamable HTTP door: right for call answers.** The tool calls the bridge with exactly two arguments when `actionConfirmationElicitorFor` answers `undefined`, and `confirmationHandOff` then carries no `elicitConfirmation` key, so the #34202 path is taken unchanged. `handleHttpRequest` still builds a fresh server per POST with `enableJsonResponse: true`; the capable-client HTTP pin is green. Not byte-identical: the `run_action` and `resume_run` tool descriptions each gain one sentence, for every client on both doors. That is a declared change and the sentence is conditional ("when your client supports elicitation and this connection can carry it"), so it is true on HTTP.
- **Fail direction: right.** An unreadable result, an error answer, a thrown elicitor, an aborted call and a closed connection all read as `cancel`; nothing in the branch can turn a failure into a run. An answer after the bound cannot run anything: the awaited promise has already settled as `timed_out` and the refusal has been returned.
- **Public surface: right.** `@objectstack/mcp` gains three value exports and four types; `McpActionBridge.runAction` / `resumeRun` gain an optional third parameter, which no existing implementer has to supply.
- **Invocation row: right.** An elicited refusal returns the `refused` shape and writes no row, as a hand-off writes none; an accepted call writes the row every admitted call writes.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` holds: nothing an author or consumer could do before is refused now on a path that was not already a non-run (the hand-off ran nothing either). `Metadata-protocol: semantic` holds: no key is added or removed; what `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` does at the stdio MCP door changes. The rule asks at least `minor` on each package the diff moves; the changeset gives `minor` to `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/mcp`, the only two moved. Match. `Check Changeset` is green. No migration entry and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed: the change is not breaking and removes nothing authorable. ADR-0011's confirmation note already states the elicit step, so no ADR edit is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 (HTTP door): answered.** Ruling 6909391261, Q1 = A: stdio only; HTTP keeps the hand-off until #34321, which is open and carries the HTTP half. The PR matches.
- **Open question 2 (cancel / timeout): answered.** Same ruling, Q2 = A: refuse, no email. The contract on `main` (rule 4) says the same; correction 6909454219 withdraws the claim's misquote. The PR matches. The card body's "fall back to the hold-and-email path" is superseded and should be read with the ruling.
- **Deviation, no-service sentence not restored: accepted with a carrier owed.** Contract step 3.3 says the message tells the person to use a client that supports confirmation, or to act in the app. The message still omits the first half. The ruling allows a door-aware follow-up "the area may file"; the dev report lists it `carrier: none`. It needs a card before #33712 closes, or the contract and the door disagree with nothing tracking it.
- **Deviation, tool descriptions in `mcp-http-tools.ts`: accepted.** #34209 edits the same descriptions and the same `*-33690` pin files; whichever lands second merges `main`. No conflict of meaning: #34209 retires `confirm` text, this PR adds the in-client sentence.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed`: the carrier needs widening.** #34210 as written covers the hand-off, `no_confirmation_service` and `service_account` only. It does not mention elicitation or `declined` / `cancelled` / `timed_out`, and has no comment adding them. Widen #34210 (both skill files it names) or file a sibling.
- **Deviation, HTTP pins replaced by elicitor pins over the in-memory pair: accepted**, given Q1.
- **Close note owed on #33712** (ruling): hosted HTTP users keep the email path until #34321. The PR is `Part of`, so the card stays open; correct.
- **`security_findings: none` in the dev report: not upheld.** See ④, findings 1 and 2.
- Out of scope, noted for the area: `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` and `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx` still teach `confirm: true` for these tools. That predates this PR (#34202); no carrier was found for the docs pages, as distinct from the skills.

### ④ Design judgment

The change makes the spec's own declared step real at the one door that can carry it, and takes nothing away at any other. It follows the contract's order and its answer table. Findings:

1. **should-fix — `run_action` dispatches on the admission read before the question.** The contract's rule 2 is met at the moment of asking. On `accept`, `run_action` dispatches on the subject and caller-scope verdict read before the question, while `resume_run` in this same PR re-reads them after the answer (through `continueAdmittedRun`), so the two doors differ. Rule: an elicited `accept` should dispatch on a subject and verdict read after the answer, as `resume_run` does. The mechanism went to the seat privately.
2. **should-fix — the record title in the question.** (a) The subject is a row a read returned; `record-title.ts` states that such a row's title is read with `servedRecordTitle` and never re-derived, and names what re-deriving with `resolveRecordTitle` gets wrong. The diff calls `resolveRecordTitle`. (b) Rule: the question names the record by the title the caller-scope read served, bounded and neutralised, and the id stays unambiguous. The mechanism went to the seat privately.
3. **nit — the bound against client timeouts.** Five minutes is a defensible door bound and the contract leaves it to the door. The server sends no progress while the question is open, so a client whose own tool-call timeout is shorter ends the call first; that reads as `cancelled` and runs nothing, which is safe. Acceptance against a real Claude Code or Codex client is unmeasured (the card says so too). Follow-up, not a fix here.
4. **nit — pins not present.** No pin sends a late `accept` after the bound, cancels the tool call while the question is open, or sends `initialize` batched with `tools/call` to the HTTP door. Each fails closed by construction in the code read; the batched case rests on the SDK, which was not readable here.
5. **nit — changeset prose.** The `Metadata-protocol:` line in the changeset carries the claim's instruction to the dev ("The dev confirms the level against the diff and, if it holds, adds the PR body's `Skills-docs:` line."), which ships in `CHANGELOG.md`. The PR body carries the same parenthetical.
6. **nit — PR body, 维护者速读 line 6** still says both questions await the maintainer. Ruling 6909391261 answered them; the line is stale.
7. **Observation for the contract, not a finding on this PR.** The question names the action, the object and the record, as step 3.1 lists; it does not show the call's `params` or a resume's `values`, which a hand-off does carry to the app. The person accepts without seeing them. That is the contract's text, so any change is a spec amendment.

Spoof, replay and race: the answer is read from the SDK's pending-request table for the one request the server sent on the connection it was sent on; a second or late answer finds no pending request. ADR-0011 already states what an `accept` proves: that the client answered. Nothing in this PR weakens or strengthens that.

No must-fix. Findings 1 and 2 earn a delta review of their fix.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `3557594b65debd8755e4e2c90385d781706f5540`
Reviewer: review-a (S3) · 2026-11-16T06:53Z
Implemented-by: S3 area dev (`session_01QsR2jTEivi2wogPpeo3xd5`)
Reviewed-by: `session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM`
Diff base: `4bd3f240` (the head's main parent); 9 files, +845/−19.

### What holds

- **Step order (contract step 2).** `confirmAdmittedAction` asks only after `admitResolvedAction` passed and after `refuseDeniedSubjectBeforeHandOff`, so a call refused anyway is never asked. `resumeActionRun` asks only after `refuseUnresumableAdmittedRun` (steps 4 and 5), which now returns the subject it read so the question can carry the title. Pinned: "a record the caller cannot read is refused 404 before anyone is asked".
- **Accept runs once, nothing handed off (step 4).** An elicited accept returns `'accepted'` and `runResolvedAction` falls through to the same `dispatchAdmittedAction` every admitted call takes; the hand-off is the `else` arm, never both. The next call is asked again (pinned). Resume accept continues the parked run with the call's values (pinned).
- **Refusal reasons.** decline / cancel / timed_out map to `declined` / `cancelled` / `timed_out` through the existing `confirmationRefusalOf` (428, `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`); a throwing elicitor reads `cancelled`. All three are members of the closed `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REFUSAL_REASONS`; no new reason is minted. Rule 5 holds: the caller's `confirm` is not read on this branch.
- **Service account (rule 6).** `aiDoorConfirmation` returns `refuse` for an AI service account at admission, so `confirmationHandOff` is never reached and the elicitor is never called; pinned at both doors ("refused before anyone is asked").
- **Non-capable and HTTP callers are unchanged.** `actionConfirmationElicitorFor` returns `undefined` unless the client advertised form-mode `elicitation` on this server's `initialize` and `extra.sendRequest` exists; the tools then call the bridge with exactly the two arguments they passed before. On Streamable HTTP the per-request server never read `initialize`, so it hands off (pinned with a real client that did advertise it). This is the maintainer ruling Q1=A (#33712 comment 6909391261).
- **Cancel / timeout refuse, not fall back (Q2=A).** Matches the same ruling and the spec text; the PR does not edit `packages/spec`.
- **The answer is `action` alone (step 3.1).** The loose result schema reads `action` only; a form payload the SDK would reject cannot turn an accept into a failure (pinned). The abort check precedes the timeout check, so a dropped connection reads `cancel`, not `timed_out` (pinned).
- **The timeout is a door constant** (`ACTION_CONFIRMATION_ELICITATION_TIMEOUT_MS`, five minutes), not an authorable key, as the contract asks the door to name its bound.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: no` holds: no schema, contract or authorable key moves; the new exports are additive runtime/mcp API (minor on both, as the changeset says). `Metadata-protocol: semantic` holds: what `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` does at the stdio door changes, its shape does not.
- **Ablations** in the PR body cover each new branch (both elicit branches, the tool's elicitor, the account refusal, the capability check), each red when removed.

### Must

None.

### Should

These are the contract record's findings 1 and 2, which I verified against the diff. Each earns a delta review of its fix, and I'd fix both in this PR before landing.

1. **`run_action` dispatches on the admission read before the question.** On `accept`, `confirmAdmittedAction` returns `'accepted'` and `dispatchAdmittedAction` receives the same `admission`, with its subject and caller-scope verdict, that was read before the person was asked. `resume_run` in this PR re-reads them after the answer. Rule: an elicited `accept` dispatches on a subject and verdict read after the answer, as `resume_run` does, with a pin. The mechanism went to the seat privately.
2. **The record title in the question.** `actionConfirmationElicitSubject` calls `resolveRecordTitle` on a row a read returned; `packages/objectql/src/record-title.ts` says such a row's title is read with `servedRecordTitle` and never re-derived. Rule: the question names the record by the served title, bounded and neutralised, and the id stays unambiguous, with a pin. The mechanism went to the seat privately.
3. `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` needs its card number before ACCEPT (the line becomes `follow-up #N`). #34210 covers the hand-off, `no_confirmation_service` and `service_account` only; it needs widening to the elicit step and `declined` / `cancelled` / `timed_out`, or a sibling card.
4. The PR body's 维护者速读 line 6 still asks the maintainer to rule on HTTP elicitation and on cancel/timeout. Both were ruled (Q1=A, Q2=A, #33712 comment 6909391261). The seat's final copy should replace it with what the maintainer has left to do.

### Nits

1. The question names the action, object and record but not the call's `params` (or a resume's `values`). That is what contract step 3.1 asks for, so it is not a defect here; whether the person should see them is a contract question for #33712.
2. The changeset's `Metadata-protocol:` line carries the claim's instruction to the dev ("The dev confirms the level…"), which would ship in `CHANGELOG.md`; the PR body has the same parenthetical.
3. No pin covers a late `accept` after the bound, a tool call cancelled mid-question, or `initialize` batched with `tools/call` on HTTP. Each fails closed in the code read.
4. #34209 collides with this PR on `mcp-http-tools.ts` and the `*-33690` pins; whichever lands second owes a clean merge and a delta read.

Board items for the area, not this diff: the no-service message still omits "use a client that supports confirmation" (contract step 3.3) and needs a carrier card before #33712 closes; #33712's close note owes "hosted HTTP users keep the email path until #34321"; `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` and `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx` still teach `confirm: true` (predates this PR, no carrier found).

### Gates

51 check runs at this head: 35 success, 16 skipped (the ui, docs, dogfood and temporal jobs the path filter leaves out, the opt-in jobs, and the queue-only and schedule-only verdicts), 0 failed or pending. Test Core 8/8, Build Core, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset and the PR-body guards are green. The PR body records 70/70 derived dispatch gates run, all exit 0, and a clean `merge-tree` against `origin/main`.

The contract-review record for the `semantic` face is comment 6909611877 (PASS, the same two should-fix findings).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c3019504e02664d6e96c940a28dfdaebb28d0198`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/mcp/src/action-confirmation-elicitation.ts, packages/mcp/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-action-confirmation-handoff-33690.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-confirmation-handoff-33690.test.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts, packages/objectql/src/record-title.ts (read in the cited code, not reviewed)

Delta review of the record on head `3557594b`. This head is the dev's `736e6595ffa1038be087b970ca8590d0a2a6776c` with `main` merged in; review-a measured the PR's net diff at both as patch-id equal (`git diff 4bd3f240 736e6595` against `git diff 4c0cf65f c3019504`), and this record takes that as given. The delta read is `git diff 3557594b 736e6595` (commits `86f49031`, `ee1b4ede`, `736e6595`), plus dev report 6911027896 on the card. Check-runs: on `736e6595` every run is `success` (35) or `skipped` (16). On this head, at the time of this record, 14 are `success`, 18 `skipped` and 20 still `in_progress` (Test Core 1 to 8, Check Changeset, type check and lint families); none has failed. The gate verdicts on this head are therefore not yet all in, and this record does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`run_action` after an elicited `accept`: right.** `runResolvedAction` now calls `admitResolvedAction` a second time after the answer (every gate, the service-account step and the subject load), then `subjectVerdictRefusal` on that fresh subject, and dispatches on the fresh admission only. A refusal on the second read returns the `refused` shape: nothing runs, no invocation row. The person is still asked once; the second pass does not re-enter `confirmAdmittedAction`. The pre-question verdict is the same function, factored out, so the hand-off path is unchanged in behaviour.
- **`resume_run` after an elicited `accept`: right.** `resumeAdmissionRefusal` is asked again for the admitting action, then `continueAdmittedRun` re-reads the subject and the screen pause as before.
- **Title source: right.** `actionConfirmationElicitSubject` reads `servedRecordTitle`; `resolveRecordTitle` is no longer imported. A row served without its title yields no title, and the id still names the record.
- **Question text: right.** One labelled line per fact in a fixed order, the record id line before the title line. Free text (label, title) has unshown characters turned to spaces, the markup set dropped, whitespace collapsed, and is cut at 80 code points; names and ids keep their characters, show an unshown character as U+FFFD, and are cut at 200. No value can start a line, so the id line is always the door's own.
- **Accept-set otherwise unchanged.** The answers table, the refusal reasons, the non-capable path and the HTTP door are untouched by the delta.
- **Public surface.** `@objectstack/mcp` gains three more value exports: `confirmationQuestionText`, `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_QUESTION_TEXT_MAX`, `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_QUESTION_ID_MAX`. Additive.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still matching: `minor` on `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/mcp`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. The three added exports are covered by `minor` and are named in the changeset. `Check Changeset` was green on `736e6595` and is still running on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Should-fix 1 and 2 of the first record: both answered in the tree** (see ④).
- **Nit 4: answered.** New pins: an `accept` after the bound is not read; a tool call cancelled while the question is open reads `cancel`; `initialize` batched with a tool call on the HTTP door is refused by the transport before any tool runs. The last one replaces what the first record had to take on trust about the SDK.
- **Nit 5: answered in the changeset.** The instruction parenthetical is gone. The PR body's `Metadata-protocol:` line still carries it; the two lines agree on the kind, `semantic`.
- **Nit 6: answered.** 维护者速读 line 6 now cites ruling 6909391261.
- **`Skills-docs`: carrier widened.** #34210's body now covers the in-client question and `declined` / `cancelled` / `timed_out`. The PR body line names it; the changeset line still reads `follow-up owed` with the file path. Same carrier, two wordings.
- **Dev flag, "the resume re-gate has no dedicated pin": upheld as a nit** (④, item 3).
- From the first record, outside this diff: #34325 now carries the door-aware no-service message (contract step 3.3), and the #33712 close note about hosted HTTP users and #34321 is owed at landing.

### ④ Design judgment
